answer: A staking bond makes each identity expensive: an agent must lock funds before it can earn, so a Sybil farmer pays the bond for every fake account. Like a quill that only writes when inked, reputation accrues slowly through attested work, and a raven carrying a forged letter is caught when its history does not match its claims. Reaching the zenith of rewards requires sustained, verifiable contribution, so faking many identities costs more than running one honest one.
